name: quality-v1
note: The fixed prompt set for the real-model quality reference (issue I-031).
input_ids are authoritative and were produced by the checkpoint's own tokenizer
(/home/gary/models/qwen38-flash-next-nvfp4) with add_special_tokens=False; `text` is what a human reads.
reference_trace.py --tokenizer re-derives the ids from the text and fails if a tokenizer
change moved them, so the reference can never silently become a different token stream.
Batch size is 1 and one prompt is one forward pass: no padding, no masking choices.
Each prompt is a domain the serving path actually sees, not a benchmark suite: no task
scores are extracted from these, only KL, dPPL and per-layer drift.

prompts.text: Every measurement in this project has to carry its conditions with it, or it becomes a rumour. A bandwidth without a topology is a rumour. A latency without a queue depth is a rumour. A throughput without a batch model is the loudest rumour of all, because it is the one people put in a table next to someone else's number and then argue about it for a week. So: state the parallel strategy, state the batch model, state the cache state, and state what was running on the machine while you measured. If you cannot state those four things, the number is not evidence, it is decoration. The second rule is that a reference must be reproducible by a stranger, on a different day, without asking you a question. If the only person who can regenerate a fixture is the person who wrote it, then the fixture is a file and not a reference. The third rule is that a tolerance is a measurement too. Setting a threshold tighter than the noise of the thing you are comparing against does not make the check stricter; it makes the check random, and random checks are turned off within a sprint. So measure the noise floor first, write it down, and put the threshold above it with a margin you can defend out loud.
